entities.title: The calendar is its own repository and Worker
entities.summary: It is not part of innkaupalistinn.net, and shares no database with it.
entities.context: An earlier plan linked the calendar to Innkaupalistinn through a shared family database and a sign-in hub inside the shopping app.
entities.decision: A repository and Worker of its own at icelander.net/calendar, signing in through icelander.net's login service.
entities.rationale: The owner asked for this repository and for the same Google sign-in the rest of icelander.net uses.

entities.title: Sign-in is the icelander.net login service
entities.summary: Google (and the other providers) through the vendored icelander-auth library and an ACCOUNTS service binding; no provider code here.
entities.context: The owner asked for the same Google login mechanism Snekkjó uses.
entities.decision: App id calendar, cookie calendar_session on /calendar, callback https://icelander.net/calendar/auth/callback.
entities.rationale: One sign-in for icelander.net; the provider needs to know one site only.

entities.title: Light mode only
entities.decision: The client declares color-scheme light and has no dark styles.

entities.title: Nothing is hidden inside a household
entities.context: A family does not need hidden information, said the owner.
entities.decision: Every member sees every schedule in their household.

entities.title: Whether and how the calendar links to Innkaupalistinn
entities.summary: The first idea was that a family configures once for both apps. Innkaupalistinn.net is a separate domain outside icelander.net's sign-in, so the two now share nothing.
entities.context: Households exist separately in each app. Sharing them would need either innkaupalistinn.net joining the login service (a separate domain, so cookies and provider redirect URIs differ) or a household API one app calls on the other.

options.title: Keep them separate
options.consequences: A family sets up each app once; nothing to build.

options.title: Innkaupalistinn signs in through the login service too
options.consequences: One identity for both; households still separate until a sharing step is designed.
